lead: Physical media and publications as objects (books, records, discs, tapes, films, comics, periodicals, sheet music, maps and globes), organised by carrier and format, then by edition class and publisher or label collector line; titles themselves belong to the entertainment and literature taxonomies.

depts.note: Tier for everyday formats; variety for fine, limited, early and manuscript books. Titles are out of scope.

b.v: first edition, first printing > later printing > book-club or reprint
b.w: Collectors weigh the edition first; identified from the copyright page and number line.

b.v: manuscript > incunabulum > fine/private press, limited signed > trade first > reprint
b.w: Separates the collector tiers from ordinary trade copies.

b.v: Fine > Near Fine > Very Good > Good > Fair > Poor (dust jacket graded separately)
b.w: Standard antiquarian booksellers' scale (ABAA / AbeBooks usage).
Plates, maps, dust jacket, slipcase, errata slips.

b.v: fine or designer binding > contemporary binding > publisher's cloth > paper
b.w: Binding quality and whether it is original to the copy.
Signatures, inscriptions and former owners raise value; a fact of one copy.

b.v: hardback > trade paperback > mass-market
b.w: New books are first sorted by how they are bound.

s.brief: Restraint plus publisher collector lines. Keep binding/format kinds plain; attribute variants (trim size, large print, library binding, dust jacket) go into t. Publisher collector lines become archetypes or ranges (allowed in media): Penguin (Penguin Classics, Penguin Modern Classics, Clothbound Classics, Little Black Classics, Pelican), Everyman's Library, Library of America, Loeb Classical Library, Bibliothèque de la Pléiade, Reclam Universal-Bibliothek, Insel-Bücherei, Folio (Gallimard), Iwanami Bunko, Shinchōsha Bunko, Kadokawa Bunko and the light-novel bunko labels (keep only the major ones, trim the 18 Kadokawa SKU-level labels to a handful). No title lists. Sewing/knitting patterns: keep the four pattern houses as archetypes (Butterick, McCall's, Simplicity, Vogue Patterns) with vintage era note.

k.brief: Penguin Clothbound Classics, Everyman's Library, Library of America, Pléiade as collector lines.
Trade and mass-market as t; Japanese bunko and shinsho as t or archetypes; trim Kadokawa labels.

s.brief: Baby tag on board, cloth/bath and novelty books. Add archetypes for novelty mechanisms with originators (Lothar Meggendorfer movable books, Robert Sabuda / Matthew Reinhart pop-ups, Dean's Rag Books as originator of the rag book, Ladybird Books and Little Golden Books as collector series lines, Usborne 'That's not my…' touchy-feely line). No story titles as archetypes unless the book format itself is the icon.

k.brief: Pop-up, movable, lift-the-flap, sound, touch-and-feel as t; historic movable books as archetypes.
Small uniform-format children's series sold as a collectable line (Ladybird, Little Golden Books, Observer's Books, I-Spy).

s.brief: Variety. Edition class is the axis. Private and fine presses as archetypes ordered by significance: Kelmscott Press, Doves Press, Ashendene, Essex House, Golden Cockerel, Gregynog, Nonesuch, Cranach Presse, Grabhorn, Arion Press. Subscription collector publishers: Limited Editions Club, Heritage Press, Folio Society, Easton Press, Franklin Library. Modern limited signed: Subterranean Press, Suntup, Lyra's Books, Centipede Press. Fine binders: Sangorski & Sutcliffe, Zaehnsdorf, Riviere, Bayntun, Cobden-Sanderson, Paul Bonet (designer binding). Facsimile publishers: Faksimile Verlag, M. Moleiro, Akademische Druck- u. Verlagsanstalt. Add traditions where relevant (e.g. Arts and Crafts private press movement, Western fine bookbinding, marbled paper / ebru). Brand-register entries for the presses and publishers.

k.brief: Hand-set, hand-printed books from a private or fine press.
Illustrated, decoratively bound editions from subscription publishers (LEC, Folio, Easton, Franklin).
Numbered or lettered state of a trade book, signed; states (lettered, numbered, traycased) as t.
Book bound or rebound by a named binder in leather with tooling; designer bindings.
Full-colour, full-size reproduction of a manuscript or early book, often numbered.
Uncorrected proof or advance reading copy issued before publication.

s.brief: Variety, tradition-led. Incunabula (Gutenberg Bible as reference, Nuremberg Chronicle, Aldine Press, Jenson), hand-press books (Aldine octavos, Elzevir, Plantin, Baskerville, Bodoni). Manuscripts: illuminated manuscripts and single leaves (book of hours as archetype). East Asian thread-bound books (Japanese wahon/fukurotoji, ehon woodblock books; Chinese xianzhuang). Palm-leaf manuscripts (South and Southeast Asia). Add a tradition entry per binding/manuscript tradition (Japanese wahon, Chinese thread binding, Islamic manuscript and binding, Ethiopian manuscripts, palm-leaf manuscripts, Western illumination). Religious scripture as a class may cross-link F4 but stays here as book objects.

k.brief: Book printed in Europe before 1501.
Book printed on a hand press, roughly 1501–1830.
Book of hours, psalter, etc.; single leaves as t.
Handwritten codex not chiefly decorated: commonplace books, recipe manuscripts, Islamic and Ethiopian manuscripts.
Wahon, fukurotoji stab binding; woodblock ehon.
Xianzhuang stitched binding.
Small cheap popular booklet of the 16th–19th centuries.

depts.note: Organised by carrier; pressing attributes follow Discogs axes (format, size, speed, label, country, pressing plant, matrix/runout).

b.v: direct-to-disc / all-analogue > analogue reissue from master tapes > digital source
b.w: First question for audiophile buyers.

b.v: original first pressing > audiophile reissue > later or budget pressing
b.w: Identified by matrix/runout, label variant and plant (Discogs).

b.v: 200 g / 180 g > 140 g; 45 rpm audiophile cut > 33⅓ rpm
b.w: Common audiophile ladders.

b.v: Mint > Near Mint > VG+ > VG > Good/G+ > Fair/Poor (Goldmine)
b.w: Disc and sleeve graded separately.

b.v: SACD and DVD-Audio > HDCD > CD 16-bit/44.1 kHz
b.w: Measured from the disc itself.
Japanese pressings with obi are a collector tag.

s.brief: Variety. Archetypes are audiophile and collector lines, ordered by significance: Mobile Fidelity Original Master Recording and UltraDisc One-Step, Analogue Productions (UHQR, Atlantic 75, Verve 45s), Blue Note Tone Poet and Classic Vinyl series, Sheffield Lab direct-to-disc, Speakers Corner, Impex, Intervention, Craft Recordings Small Batch, Acoustic Sounds Series, Record Store Day releases; Japanese pressings with obi as a version/detail. Pressing attributes (coloured vinyl, picture disc, half-speed master, quadraphonic, gatefold, box set) go into t or dt. Merge release types into kinds by disc size. No album titles.

k.brief: 12-inch 33⅓ album; audiophile lines as archetypes.
10-inch microgroove disc (early LPs, modern EPs).
Record with an image sealed into the playing surface; shaped discs as t.

s.brief: Variety, historic carriers. Archetypes: Berliner gramophone disc, Victor / HMV Red Seal, Columbia, Edison Diamond Disc, Pathé vertical discs, Edison Amberol / Blue Amberol / Gold Moulded cylinders, Columbia and Lambert cylinders, Eva-Tone Soundsheet and Asahi Sonorama flexi-discs, Presto and Wilcox-Gay lathe discs, Voice-O-Graph, NBC Thesaurus / World transcription discs. Merge acetate and lathe-cut; keep 16-inch transcription disc as a kind (collectors own them).

Mixed. Audiophile CD/SACD lines as archetypes: MoFi Ultradisc gold CD and hybrid SACD, DCC Compact Classics gold CD, JVC XRCD, Universal SHM-CD, Sony Blu-spec CD2, Memory Tech HQCD, Analogue Productions SACD, Esoteric SACD; HDCD as t. Add MiniDisc (Sony) and Blu-ray audio (Pure Audio Blu-ray) as new kinds.

Variety for collectors, tier for blanks. Compact cassette: blank-tape archetypes by type (Type I/II/IV as t) with icons (TDK SA, TDK MA-R, Maxell XLII, Sony Metal Master, Nakamichi ZX), pre-recorded cassettes, Dolby as detail. Add reel-to-reel prerecorded tape (The Tape Project, Barclay-Crocker, Ampex), 8-track cartridge (Lear Jet Stereo 8), DAT, Digital Compact Cassette, Elcaset. Keep Playaway as the audiobook-player archetype.

depts.note: Organised by carrier; boutique labels and packaging are the collector axis. Film titles are out of scope.

b.v: boutique restoration label (Criterion, Arrow, Eureka, BFI) > studio catalogue release > budget reissue
b.w: Collectors rank by the label's restoration and extras.

b.v: Ultra HD Blu-ray > Blu-ray > DVD > LaserDisc > VHS
b.w: Resolution of the carrier.

b.v: limited box / mediabook / Steelbook > slipcover > standard case
b.w: Packaging is a collected attribute.

b.v: sealed > complete with inserts > disc only
b.w: Graded VHS (e.g. VGA/IGS) is a niche market.
Determines playability.

s.brief: Variety. Boutique labels as archetypes/ranges on DVD, Blu-ray and UHD (ordered by significance): The Criterion Collection, Arrow Video, Eureka Masters of Cinema, BFI, Indicator (Powerhouse Films), Second Sight, Kino Lorber Studio Classics, Shout! / Scream Factory, Vinegar Syndrome, Severin, 88 Films, Radiance, Umbrella / Imprint. Packaging (Steelbook, mediabook, slipcover, digipak, limited box) as t. LaserDisc: Criterion, Pioneer LD-G, MCA DiscoVision; add HD DVD, Video CD and CED as new kinds. Brand-register entries for the labels.

k.brief: RCA Capacitance Electronic Disc in caddy.

s.brief: Variety for VHS collectors (big-box, Disney clamshell 'Black Diamond', pre-cert / video nasties as versions or t), restraint for formats. Add Video 2000 and Video8/Hi8 / MiniDV as camcorder cassettes. Keep S-VHS, VHS-C, W-VHS.

k.brief: Video8, Hi8, Digital8 as t.

s.brief: Home-movie collector market. Archetypes for home-distribution lines: Castle Films, Blackhawk Films, Derann, Ken Films, Pathéscope. Add 9.5 mm (Pathé Baby) prints as a new kind. Sound/silent, colour/b&w, reel size as t.

depts.note: Organised by edition format; publisher collected-edition lines are the collector axis. Series titles are out of scope.

b.v: premium large format / Artist's Edition > omnibus > hardcover > trade > single issue
b.w: Collected editions are sorted by format first.

b.v: CGC / CBCS 10-point scale (10.0 Gem Mint … 0.5 Poor); slabbed > raw
b.w: Third-party grading dominates single-issue collecting.

b.v: first printing > later printing; cover variants (incentive ratios)
b.w: Variant and printing identified from indicia.

b.v: Golden, Silver, Bronze, Modern Age
b.w: Period is an attribute and a view, not a kind.

s.brief: Variety. Publisher collected-edition lines become archetypes: Marvel Masterworks, Marvel Omnibus, Epic Collection, DC Absolute, DC Archive Editions, DC Omnibus, Fantagraphics/IDW Artist's Edition, Image Compendium; manga labels (Jump Comics, Shōnen Magazine Comics, Shōnen Sunday Comics, kanzenban, aizōban). Bande dessinée album (Dupuis, Casterman, Dargaud, Le Lombard) as a new kind. Add manga anthology magazine (Weekly Shōnen Jump etc. as format, not titles) and dōjinshi. Single issues: grading and variants into t/dt. Trim the Kadokawa SKU labels.

k.brief: Trade paperback and tankōbon.
Absolute, Artist's Edition, kanzenban.

depts.note: Periodicals as objects; titles only as examples of a format.

b.v: first issue, complete run > single issue
b.w: Runs and first issues are the collector axis.
Newsprint and pulp paper browns; covers and centrefolds checked.

s.brief: Mixed. Keep formats plain; add pulp magazine (Argosy, Weird Tales, Amazing Stories as format exemplars) and newspaper formats as t. Part-work joins here (De Agostini, Eaglemoss, Hachette as publishers). Zine: punk and sci-fi fanzine as archetypes. Bound periodical volume: Punch, The Strand, Illustrated London News as typical bound runs.

depts.note: Organised by score type; publisher editions (Urtext, miniature scores) are the comparison axis.

b.v: Urtext / critical edition > performing edition > reprint
b.w: Players and teachers compare editions by publisher (Henle, Bärenreiter, Wiener Urtext).

b.v: full score > study score; score and parts
b.w: Matches use: conducting, study or performance.

b.v: cover art, first issue
b.w: Collectors of popular song sheets weigh illustrated covers.

s.brief: Mixed. Publisher edition lines as archetypes: G. Henle Urtext (blue covers), Bärenreiter Urtext, Wiener Urtext, Edition Peters, Breitkopf & Härtel, Schirmer's Library, Dover reprints, Eulenburg, Boosey & Hawkes Hawkes Pocket Scores, Kalmus. Merge set of parts and single part into Performance parts (t: complete set, single part). Add method or tutor book (Suzuki, Hal Leonard methods, ABRSM exam books) and popular song sheet (Victorian, Tin Pan Alley illustrated sheet music) as new kinds.

depts.note: Tier for current maps; variety for antique maps and globes, keyed to cartographer and maker.

b.v: named early cartographer, first state > later state > facsimile
b.w: Antique maps are valued by maker and state.

b.v: original hand colour > later colour > uncoloured
b.w: Dealers' standard distinction.

b.v: A / B / C grade (dealer scale)
b.w: Folds, margins, foxing.

b.v: 1:25 000 > 1:50 000 for walking
b.w: Practical choice for use maps.

s.brief: Tier. Keep national survey series as archetypes (Ordnance Survey Explorer/Landranger, IGN TOP 25/TOP 100, Nordeca, Norstedts Fjällkartan, USGS 7.5-minute quad, Harvey, Michelin); merge tear-off map pad into folded/sheet map as t. Atlases: road atlases (AA, Philip's, A-Z), reference atlases (The Times Atlas of the World, National Geographic Atlas). Trim to market-covering lines.

Variety, keyed to cartographer. Archetypes ordered by significance: Ptolemy Geographia editions, Ortelius Theatrum Orbis Terrarum, Mercator atlas, Blaeu Atlas Maior, Hondius/Jansson, John Speed, Homann, Cassini, Cary; sea charts (Waghenaer, Van Keulen, Admiralty charts); celestial atlases (Cellarius Harmonia Macrocosmica, Doppelmayr); road maps (Ogilby Britannia; mid-century oil-company road maps); pictorial and novelty maps. Add tradition entries (Dutch golden-age cartography; Japanese woodblock maps).

k.brief: Engraved or woodcut map sheet, often from a broken atlas; state and colouring as t.
Strip and folded road maps incl. oil-company giveaways.

s.brief: Mixed. Trim the Replogle SKU list (17 models + ranges) and Columbus ranges to the main lines as archetypes (Columbus Duorama/Duo, Replogle, Bellerby & Co handmade, Waypoint, National Geographic). Antique globes as variety: Blaeu, Coronelli, Cary, Newton, Smith, Holbrook, Schedler; terrestrial/celestial pairs; pocket globes. Illuminated, relief, gemstone as t. Globe stand joins here from accessories.

depts.note: Sleeves, cases and boxes made for one medium; archival quality is the main ladder.

b.v: acid-free / Mylar (polyester) > polypropylene > PVC or paper
b.w: Polyester and acid-free board protect long-term; PVC degrades.
Sized for the specific format (Golden/Silver/Current Age comic, 12-inch jacket, CD).

s.brief: Tier. Market brands: BCW, Ultra PRO, E. Gerber (Mylites), Brodart; bookbinders' boxes (Bayntun) as a crafted option. Add comic storage box (short and long box) as a new kind. Loose dust jacket: facsimile jackets (e.g. Facsimile Dust Jackets LLC) as an archetype if sourced.

k.brief: Polypropylene vs Mylar as t; size class by comic age.

s.brief: Tier. Market brands: Mobile Fidelity, Nagaoka, Sleeve City, Discogs-favoured anti-static sleeves; CD jewel case types (standard, slimline, double) as t. Add record storage box/crate only if clearly media-specific, otherwise leave to Furniture.
